public_rationale: He said that 'every single AI startup without exception' fails to improve its margins. A universal claim falls to one credible counterexample. TechCrunch, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Cursor, a startup he names in the same passage, ran at negative gross margins until recently. Its own Composer model, launched in November 2025, and cheaper models helped it reach slight gross-margin profit. Sacra estimated that Replit's gross margin rose from -14% in April 2025 to 23% in July 2025. Both are estimates, not audited figures, and Replit's 2025 margins swung up and down. Still, at least one AI startup was improving its margins in the period before the post. The vaguer second sentence, 'none of them have a solution', was not graded.
limitations: The evidence is sourced press and analyst estimates, not company filings.
The Cursor report came a month after the post. Its 'until recently' leaves the timing of the improvement approximate.
Gross margin is the evaluator's reading of 'margins'.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No AI startup is improving its margins or has a solution to its economics.

statement.excerpt: None of them are improving their margins. None of them have a solution.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: Every single AI startup without exception
None of them are improving their margins
None of them have a solution
our_interpretation: Plain reading: no AI application startup (the Cursor, Harvey, Lovable type he discusses, separate from Anthropic and OpenAI) was seeing its margins get better at the time of the March 2026 post. 'Margins' is read as gross margin, the margin usually reported for these startups.
The claim is universal ('without exception'), so one credible report of an AI startup's margins improving during the recent period is enough to contradict it.
Period: the claim describes a current trend with no period named. I use 2025-01-01 to the post date (2026-03-17), which covers the 2025 and early-2026 figures he cites. This choice is flagged.
'None of them have a solution' has no testable measure and is not graded on its own. The verdict rests on the margins sentence.
criteria.support_condition: Available reporting through the post date shows no AI startup with improving gross margins, or shows margins flat or worsening across the startups for which figures exist.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reporting shows at least one AI startup whose gross margins improved during 2025 to March 2026.

evidence.excerpt: Cursor operated at negative gross margins until recently, meaning it cost more to run the product than the startup could charge for it. The introduction of a proprietary Composer model last November, along with the ability to call on less expensive models like China’s Kimi, has helped the company achieve slight gross margin profitability, the people said.
evidence.explanation: Cursor, a startup he names, had improving gross margins: from negative to slightly positive, a shift the source ties to the Composer model launched in November 2025. That falls in the period before the post. The figures come from anonymous sources.

evidence.excerpt: also improves unit economics as revenue shifts from low-margin inference to high-margin SaaS attach, with gross margins improving from negative 14% in April to 23% in July.
evidence.locator: summary paragraph on deployed internal apps
evidence.explanation: An analyst estimate that AI coding startup Replit's gross margin improved from -14% in April 2025 to 23% in July 2025, inside the period.

evidence.excerpt: Replit's gross margins have fluctuated between 36% and negative 14% in 2025, driven by the cost of accessing large language models for its coding agents.
evidence.explanation: Replit's margins swung during 2025, so the April-to-July rise may partly be a recovery. This weakens e2 as proof of a lasting improvement, but it does not show that margins were flat or falling.

evidence.excerpt: He also said that unlike many AI-powered coding companies, Replit is gross margin positive. On enterprise deals, which make up an increasing share of revenue, margins are “80% to 90%,” according to Masad.
evidence.locator: paragraph beginning 'Right now, that bet looks very smart'
evidence.explanation: The CEO's own claim that Replit is gross-margin positive, with a growing share of high-margin enterprise revenue. It is self-reported and unverified, so it is context only.
